steps.title: The big square
steps.say: Start with a square whose side is a + b. Its area is the same no matter how we count it.

steps.title: Four right triangles
steps.say: Put a right triangle with legs a and b in each corner. Each triangle has hypotenuse c.

steps.title: The tilted middle square
steps.say: The four triangles leave a tilted square in the middle. Its side is c, so its area is c².

steps.title: Count the big square
steps.say: The big square has side a + b, so its area is (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².

ops.text:
Big square area:
(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

steps.title: Count the triangles
steps.say: The four triangles each have area ab/2, so together they have area 2ab.

steps.title: What is left
steps.say: Remove the triangles from the big square and the middle square remains: c² = (a + b)² − 2ab = a² + b².

ops.text:
Middle square:
c² = (a + b)² − 2ab = a² + b²

steps.title: Why it works
steps.say: Both counts describe the same big square, so the leftover area must match: c² = a² + b².

ops.text:
Same big square,
counted two ways.
